summary: An announcement of a one-day workshop at BBN on May 21, 1973 titled Automated Resource Sharing on the ARPANET. The theme was how to move from humans manually using remote resources to processes acting on their behalf, including system-to-system tasks such as file backup.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC announces a BBN workshop about automating access to resources on the ARPANET. It lists the problems and approaches participants were invited to discuss.

subtitle: An announcement for a workshop on automating ARPANET resource sharing.

tldr.problem: The workshop asks how to make distributed ARPANET resources easier to access through processes acting for users and through system-to-system cooperation.
tldr.mechanism: Participants were invited to discuss obstacles, useful resources, experiments, accounting, security, approaches, and protocol needs.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is an invitation and agenda, not a report of workshop conclusions.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 504's status as Unknown. The RFC announces a workshop and proposes discussion topics.

sections.title: Automating Resource Sharing
sections.content: The workshop's main question is what steps could automate access to resources distributed across the ARPANET. The announcement asks how processes might act on behalf of users and how operating systems might cooperate, for example in file-system backup.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop asks how programs could access network resources for users. It also asks how computer systems could cooperate directly.

sections.title: Topics for Discussion
sections.content: The objectives include identifying obstacles to resource sharing, finding resources that could be shared, and planning experiments with prototype systems. Possible afternoon topics include multi-site services, remote access, locating resources, accounting, security, and user authentication.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants would identify what could be shared and what prevents sharing. They would also discuss finding resources, paying for use, and controlling access.

sections.title: Approaches and Protocols
sections.content:
The announcement names three possible approaches: multi-site executive programs, programming-language environments designed for sharing, and a collection of separate services presented together. It asks participants to compare their benefits and identify any common foundation.

The RFC says the workshop should discuss the kinds of activity protocols need to support, rather than produce a detailed protocol specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The workshop compares several ways to make resources available across sites. It is meant to discuss protocol needs, not write a detailed protocol.
